content:
thought
The first Sooty Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`) shows dark, irregular, soot-like patches covering the surface of a mango leaf, which is very similar to the test image. This strongly supports Sooty Mould as the classification.

Now I will view a reference image for Anthracnose to compare.

thought
The Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a leaf that is largely brown/orange with significant damage, including holes and torn edges, which is not consistent with the soot-like appearance of the test image. This reduces the likelihood of Anthracnose.

Next, I will view a reference image for Die Back.

thought
The Die Back reference image (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a severely shriveled, dried, and brown leaf, indicative of tissue death. This is completely different from the test image, which shows surface discoloration and spots on a largely intact leaf. This further reduces the likelihood of Die Back.

Now, I will view a reference image for Powdery Mildew.

thought
The Powdery Mildew reference image (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows white, powdery patches on the leaf surface. This is distinctly different from the dark, soot-like appearance in the test image. This rules out Powdery Mildew.

At this point, Sooty Mould is still the strongest candidate. I have used 4 out of 8 reference image views. To solidify the prediction, I will now view additional reference images for Sooty Mould.

thought
The second Sooty Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`) also displays dark, irregular patches, resembling a sooty film, on the surface of a mango leaf, consistent with the test image. This further strengthens the classification of Sooty Mould.

I have used 5 out of 8 reference image views. I will view another Sooty Mould reference image.

thought
The third Sooty Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_288.jpg`) again shows very similar characteristics to the test image: dark, irregular, soot-like patches on the leaf surface.

I have used 6 out of 8 reference image views. I am very confident in Sooty Mould. I will use the remaining two views to check more Anthracnose images to ensure there is no overlap that I missed.

thought
The second Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_24.jpg`) shows distinct brown to dark brown lesions, some with a slightly sunken appearance, primarily along the veins of a green leaf. This is quite different from the diffuse, soot-like covering observed in the test image.

I have used 7 out of 8 reference image views. I will use the last view for another Anthracnose image to be absolutely certain.
